'''trans-.''' [= F. ''trans-'', ''tré-'', OF. ''trans-'', ''tres-'' = Sp. Pg. ''trans-'', ''tras-'' = It. ''trans-'', ''tras-'', < L. ''trans-'', prefix, ''trans'', prep., across, over, beyond, on the other side of, in comp. across, over, through, through and through, beyond. Before a consonant the form varies between ''trans-'' and ''tra-'', as in ''transdere'', ''tradere'' (see ''tradition'', ''tray''<sup>3</sup>), ''transducere'', ''traducere'' (see ''traduce''), ''translucere'', ''tralucere'', etc. (see ''tralucent'', ''translucent''); before ''s'', the form commonly becomes ''tran-'', as in ''transcendere'', for ''transscendere'' (see ''transcend''), etc. This prefix appears in E. in other forms, as ''tra-'' in ''traduce'', ''traject'', etc., ''tre-'' in the obs. Being or situated beyond the Alps, especially from Rome: as, ''transalpine'' Gaul: opposed to ''cisalpine''. Compare ''transmontane''.

'''II.''' ''n.'' A native or an inhabitant of a country beyond the Alps, generally with reference to Rome.

'''transandine''' (trȧns-an′din), ''a.'' [< ''trans-'' + ''Andes'' + ''-ine''<sup>1</sup>.] Across the Andes; to or on the other side of the Andes: as, ''transandine'' explorations.

'''transanimate''' (trȧns-an′i-māt), ''v. t.''; pret. and pp. ''transanimated'', ppr. ''transanimating''. [< ''trans-'' + ''animate''.] To animate by the conveyance of a soul to another body. ''Dean King'', Sermon, Nov., 1608. [Rare.]

'''transanimation''' (trȧns-an-i-mā′shon), ''n.'' [= It. ''transanimazione''; as ''transanimate'' + ''-ion''.] Transmigration of the soul; metempsychosis; also, any doctrine or theory of reincarnation (as in the following extract).
